title: Crowd Behaviour Laboratory: Deindividuation and ESIM
summary: Set up one fictional crowd event five ways and read the result twice: once as a deindividuation account would, once as the elaborated social identity model would.
learningObjectives: State what a generic deindividuation account and the elaborated social identity model each predict about crowd action.
Explain why the two accounts disagree about the patterning of crowd behaviour rather than about its existence.
Describe how indiscriminate treatment can create the shared category it is responding to.
Distinguish anonymity amplifying a salient norm from anonymity removing restraint.
Identify a case in which the deindividuation description fits the evidence better, and say why that keeps the argument live.
privacy: Every setting and judgement is held in the browser tab only and discarded when the page is left; nothing is saved, stored or transmitted, and no score or judgement about the person using it is produced.
accessibilityNotes: All controls are native radios in labelled fieldsets and labelled selects, and nothing is timed. The target chart is hidden from assistive technology and paired with a sentence giving all four shares, the even-spread reference and the selectivity value; the police-line bar is drawn differently but every share is printed beside its bar and restated in words. The even-spread reference is a dashed rule and a printed label, never colour alone. The section table marks participation with a Yes or No column, with the heavier rule as a redundant second cue. Every change is announced through the shell's polite live region, including which preset was loaded and what it produced. Headings run h1 to h5 without skipping, focus moves to the laboratory heading when it opens, the section-by-section table sits in a scrollable wrapper inside a collapsed details element, targets are at least 2.75rem, forced-colours rules are provided, and the layout is usable at 320px and at classroom-projector widths.
readmeTopic: The same crowd, policed two ways: participation and target selection move independently, and only one account predicts each
simulationNotes: Marlow Bridge and Calder Green are inventions and no real event, policing operation, organisation or person is described; nothing here is evidence for either account, and the model produces the patterns it was built to produce. Nothing is random. Six sections of the crowd carry invented baselines - residents 0.20, campaign regulars 0.40, stallholders 0.12, students 0.28, families 0.04, and a handful who came for a confrontation 0.88. A section takes part when baseline plus unity times legitimacy plus a norm shift reaches 0.60, where unity is 0.10 for differentiated policing, 0.55 for indiscriminate policing without a common category and 1.00 with one; legitimacy is 0.12 when the response is read as reasonable and 0.50 when it is read as unfair; and the norm shift is plus 0.18 for a police-line-only norm, zero for no shared norm and minus 0.45 when confrontation is out of bounds. A section is inside the category once unity reaches 0.55, except the handful who came for a confrontation, who are absorbed only at unity 1.00. Target weights are set by the norm and reshaped by identifiability: where a norm is in play anonymity sharpens it (each weight raised to the power 1.35 and renormalised) rather than broadening it, which is the direction the social identity model of deindividuation effects predicts; where there is no shared norm anonymity moves the weights 40 per cent towards an even spread. Selectivity is the summed absolute deviation of the four shares from 0.25 divided by 1.5, and the disinhibition index is 0.2 or 0.5 for identifiability plus the participation count over 12; both are teaching devices invented for this page and neither is a published measure. The four presets produce, in order: 1 of 6 taking part with selectivity 0.84 and disinhibition 0.28; 6 of 6 with selectivity 0.84 and disinhibition 0.70; 2 of 6 with selectivity 0.08 and disinhibition 0.67; and 1 of 6 with selectivity 0.37 and disinhibition 0.58.
